title: spec review: H3b v3: wire decision routes into the daemon (spec reviews T-0430 and T-0434 folded in) — build_ctx lives in daemon.py (no import cycle), coalesced held packets carry one section per non-routine held child, dedup before any gate evidence and no suite run inside tick, gh pr create failures retried then held, cursor per goal with cursor_at_launch per record
spec:
Replaces T-0433 (superseded) after spec review T-0434. Build on goal/T-0353 at df2ae89 (H3a decision.py, H2 launch attribution, H4 reservations and notify-once helper, H7 failure kinds and signatures, H6 acceptance gate, G7 v4 auto fix rounds, G8 semantic triggers are merged). Handover sections 3 and 4.

1. Context builder placement (T-0434 risk 1): daemon.build_ctx(point) lives in orchestrator/daemon.py, which already imports planner_runs and decision at top level; planner_runs never imports daemon. planner_runs.run(point, ctx) takes the built ctx as an argument (keep a ctx=None default that builds an empty ctx so old callers and tests keep working). build_ctx reuses the daemon helpers in place (_test_ids, _rejecting_reviews, _path_in_scope, failure_kind, failure_signature, changed_paths) and adds daemon.touch_areas(task). It fills every field decision.route reads (orchestrator/decision.py lines 84-148), never leaving a required field absent:
- common: routes = pool.toml [planner.routes]; infra_failure_kind = "quota" | "auth" | "unavailable" when the pool reports a cooldown or usage-limit reason for the account or executor involved, or pipeline.failure_kind is quota or permissions; else None (present, None); premium_launches = count of escalate launches recorded for this goal.
- held (per held task): failing_ids from resume_hint.failures via the same extraction auto_fix_round uses; in_scope_review_comments = the same check auto_fix_round performs; auto_fix_rounds_used = lineage count of constraints.auto_round; auto_fix_rounds = [daemon].auto_fix_rounds; failure_signature = daemon.failure_signature(task); signature_repeated = signature equals an earlier lineage signature (H7 logic); spec_review_request_changes = count of spec_review tasks with inputs[0] in the lineage and verdict request_changes; blocked_scouts = scout ids under the goal with status blocked; touches_auth, touches_migrations, touches_interfaces, touches_data_deletion = daemon.touch_areas(task) mapping the changed paths and added lines of the task diff against four area tables in pool.toml [review.areas] (auth: auth, authz, permission, token, session paths and patterns; migrations: migrations or schema paths, ALTER/CREATE TABLE; interfaces: public API, cli, mcp tool definitions, exported symbols; data_deletion: DROP, DELETE FROM, rm -rf, shutil.rmtree, os.remove); defaults shipped; an unavailable diff sets all four True (fail closed).
- scouts_done: goal_complexity = the goal task complexity; scout_count and all_scouts_posted from the goal scout children; blocked_scouts as above; security_trigger = any goal scope path matches [review].security_paths; semantic_trigger = goal spec or scope matches [review].semantic_patterns or semantic_paths (G8 lists).
- closable: all_children_merged = every execute child of the goal is done with merged_into set (fix rounds included); gate_state = "green" when the goal branch head sha equals the sha recorded by the last successful orchestrator.merge into that goal branch (merge runs tests-green before fast-forwarding, so that head is gate-verified); "red" when the last recorded merge attempt for that head failed its gate; else "unknown". build_ctx and tick never run a test suite (T-0434 risk 3); an unknown gate_state routes closable to investigate, never to a routine close.
Test: test_ctx_fields_complete_for_each_kind asserts decision.route on a built ctx never returns an unknown reason for held, scouts_done and closable points.

2. Coalesced held packets (T-0434 risk 2): per tick and per goal, every held execute child is routed individually with its own ctx. Routine ones get auto_fix_round in that tick and never enter a packet. The non-routine ones (investigate or escalate) are coalesced into one launch for the goal: the packet carries one section per non-routine held task (task id, hold_reason, failure kind, failure signature, failing ids, branch, head sha, route and reason for that task), the goal route is the highest severity among them (escalate over investigate), and the launch runs on that route's tier. The claim record lists the task ids covered. A blocked scout or a security hold launches in the same tick as its own point. Unrelated goals never share a packet. Test: test_two_held_siblings_one_packet_non_routine_sections: one child routine-fixable (failing ids in scope, rounds left) and one escalate-worthy (touches_auth) under one goal in one tick produce exactly one auto fix round for the first, exactly one launch on the premium tier whose packet contains only the second task's section and whose claim record lists only the second id.

3. Routine close: a deterministic close guarded like every other stage. Order is fixed: (a) compute state_version and check _blocked and the existing goal claim first; an identical state_version never proceeds (test_dedup_precedes_gate_state asserts no merge-record read and no side effect happen when the state is already claimed); (b) require gate_state green from recorded merge evidence only; (c) stamp(goal_id, "closed_at") under bus.locked() before any side effect; (d) effects, each idempotent and each checked by evidence before running: retrospective entry written once (record script with facts from bus state, or the no-new-learning marker; skip when an entry for the goal id exists), the PR opened only if the goal has no recorded pr_url and gh pr list shows none for the branch, the GOAL result posted once (skip when result present). A crash between stamp and effects is reconciled on the next tick by re-checking each effect's evidence. gh pr create failure handling (T-0434 risk 4): a non-zero gh exit records pr_error (first 300 chars of stderr) and pr_attempts on the goal task, notifies once per transition (H4 helper), never counts toward gave_up, and is retried on later ticks with backoff doubling from [planner.routes].close_retry_base_s (default 60) up to [planner.routes].close_retry_max (default 3 attempts); after the last attempt the goal is held with hold_reason "pr_open_failed" and the retrospective entry and GOAL result still stand (they do not depend on the PR). Test: test_pr_create_failure_retries_then_holds (gh mocked to fail: three ticks with the clock advanced past the backoff, three attempts, one notification, hold_reason pr_open_failed, entry and result present exactly once).
investigate: launch on [planner.routes].investigate_tier; escalate: launch on the premium tier. Route, reason, evidence, cheaper_steps and covered task ids go into the claim record (H2 fields). [planner.routes].enabled = false restores the per-point escalation.

4. One claim scheme: coalesced launches are recorded as kind "goal" with payload_key = state_version (sha12 over sorted (task id, status, hold_reason, merged_into, last event seq) of the goal children); old per-point records remain readable history; new launches for held and scouts_done use the goal record only; _blocked and the gave_up rule apply to the goal record; the module docstring documents the scheme. An identical state_version never launches twice.

5. Cursor (T-0434 risk 5): the processed-event cursor is one per-goal value in planner_runs.json (key cursors[goal_id]). Each launch record carries cursor_at_launch = the cursor value the packet was built from. The per-goal cursor advances only after the launch is recorded as started (claim written and process spawned); an infra failure leaves it so the retry rebuilds the same packet. Infra failures (auth, quota, service unavailable markers in stderr or exit) set a pool cooldown with reason, do not count toward gave_up, and notify once per transition (H4 helper).

6. Soft premium budget: exceeding [planner.routes].premium_launches_soft_per_goal still launches and records exception: true with the reason.

Tests in tests/test_planner_runs.py and tests/test_daemon.py: test_ctx_fields_complete_for_each_kind, test_routine_hold_launches_no_model, test_two_held_siblings_one_packet_non_routine_sections, test_closable_all_merged_closes_without_launch, test_closable_routine_is_idempotent_across_ticks (three ticks: one PR, one result, one entry), test_closable_gate_state_from_merge_record_never_runs_suite, test_dedup_precedes_gate_state, test_pr_create_failure_retries_then_holds, test_investigate_uses_smaller_tier, test_escalate_uses_premium_tier_with_reason, test_same_state_version_never_relaunches, test_two_goals_two_packets, test_cursor_advances_only_after_launch_start, test_auth_failure_cools_account_without_gave_up, test_soft_budget_exceeded_still_launches_with_exception, test_routes_disabled_restores_per_point_launch, test_touch_areas_fail_closed_without_diff. Every gh, git and process launch in tests is mocked. Keep every existing test green; .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh exits 0; git add -A and commit with the task id; report sha and failures only.
acceptance: tests/test_planner_runs.py and tests/test_daemon.py: test_ctx_fields_complete_for_each_kind, test_routine_hold_launches_no_model, test_two_held_siblings_one_packet_non_routine_sections, test_closable_all_merged_closes_without_launch, test_closable_routine_is_idempotent_across_ticks, test_closable_gate_state_from_merge_record_never_runs_suite, test_dedup_precedes_gate_state, test_pr_create_failure_retries_then_holds, test_investigate_uses_smaller_tier, test_escalate_uses_premium_tier_with_reason, test_same_state_version_never_relaunches, test_two_goals_two_packets, test_cursor_advances_only_after_launch_start, test_auth_failure_cools_account_without_gave_up, test_soft_budget_exceeded_still_launches_with_exception, test_routes_disabled_restores_per_point_launch, test_touch_areas_fail_closed_without_diff pass
planner_runs.py has no import of daemon at module scope or inside functions; build_ctx and touch_areas are defined in daemon.py

every launch record carries route, reason, evidence, cheaper_steps, state_version, cursor_at_launch and the covered task ids; the per-goal cursor lives in planner_runs.json cursors[goal_id]; the routine close stamps closed_at before any side effect and never runs a test suite inside tick
pool.toml documents [review.areas] defaults and [planner.routes] close_retry_base_s and close_retry_max; the planner_runs module docstring documents the goal-record claim scheme
Existing tests pass; .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh exits 0 in the worktree
